He who is served by the hosts of perfected ones (*siddha*) and monks whose impurities have been removed;
he whose form is stainless, like the radiance of the dawn, so that the reality may be known;
he who is adorned here with qualities such as omniscience and possesses a body of adamant (*vajradeha*).
May it endure as a source of the bliss of peace, benefiting all sentient beings without exception—

this renowned place in the world, consisting of various jewels, a delightful and most wonderful site with vast sacred shrines, the abode of the Three Jewels, adorned with glorious monasteries and the like. || 2 ||

Through the offering of foods, the drawing of mandalas, the presentation of great assemblies for the community, and through the diligent practice of meditation, the recitation of scriptures, the instruction of teachers, and excellent sacrificial sessions; and by bringing to fulfillment the needs of the poor, the helpless, the distressed, kinsmen, well-wishers, and friends—

O you for whom there is no satiety with whatever guests arrive— be they followers of various philosophical systems, practitioners of virtuous vows, and so forth— even I am not capable of recounting the virtues of you who cause the Dharma to be written down, [a Dharma] which exists in as many distinct forms as there are divisions within the Buddhist doctrine.
Dharma himself, overcome by the power of your garland of flames, came of his own accord for refuge out of fear of it; having heard of your fame, he—
being without rival and fearless— conquered him through the virtues of your universal friendship and so forth.

Who indeed could be equal to him who sacrifices for the sake of Dharma, or what praise could there be for him? The moon, having become ashamed by the increasing marks of merit— which rival the sky and its moonbeams— seeks, it is said, to hide itself within the depths of the water.

I know you to be the foremost ocean of jewels consisting of the explanations of the white [teachings] of the Sugata, from which proceeds the happiness of all beings belonging to the illustrious lineage of Sānvaya. Your son, the illustrious Sahānu, is likewise a treasury for awakening that entire [lineage].
Even though he had not studied the scriptures, the author was a man of merit who composed treatises;

he, whose entire people were terrified by the mass of flames from the fire of suffering—[flames] emitted from his body which was as hard as a proud diamond—was one who had gratified the illustrious Goddess of Speech. 7.
Moreover:
may he become a universal monarch of vidyādharas, fully accomplished in knowledge,
a treasury of compassion, and renowned for his jewels of excellent virtues.

Although Your nature has been described by countless hymns and by many kinds of wise men as one whose virtuous conduct is praised and expanded, You have granted me permission to praise You with only a few words.
This learned monk, the lord of many ascetics, possesses the splendor of the Buddha’s awakening;
therefore, O wise ones, you should forgive me as I speak a few words according to the power of my own intellect regarding this most wonderful scholar, Kīrtidhvaja.

May those endowed with devotion to their gurus be blessed by the merit derived from this composition concerning the Sugata, the glorious creator, whose sight is difficult for men of meager merit to obtain. (10)
